title: Top and bottom row virtual desktops are not clickable when the grid = 5 rows and panel is 52 units tall on 1440p@150% scale
line: The Pager's top and bottom rows can be clicked and hovered again in thicker panels.
explanation: PanelView treats a band along the panel's edges (thick SVG margin plus smallSpacing, 12 px in a 52 px panel) as padding and moves every event there to the nearest point inside the content area, for Fitts' law. Normal applets only get the thin margin (4 px), so the Pager reaches 8 px into that band: its whole top and bottom rows were inside it, and clicks there were moved onto the 1 px gaps between rows 1-2 and 4-5, so nothing happened. The change leaves events alone when they already land on a visible applet; events on empty padding are still moved inside as before.

commits.message:
shell/panelview: don't move events that land on an applet in the padding

Events in the panel's padding were moved inside the content area even
when an applet reached into it, so Pager rows near the edges got clicks
meant for the gaps between rows. Events on applets now stay in place.

BUG: 521271

media.caption: Master: clicking desktop 4 (top row, red circle) does nothing, desktop 1 stays current
With the fix: the same click switches to desktop 4
Master: clicking desktop 24 (bottom row) does nothing
With the fix: the same click switches to desktop 24

reviews.text: This fixes the true root cause in PanelView::containmentContainsPosition() rather than papering over it in the Pager widget. By checking whether a scene point already lands inside a visible applet item before redirecting events inward for Fitts' law, clicks and hover on Pager rows extending into the thick-margin padding band work reliably while Fitts' law redirection on empty padding is preserved. The implementation is minimal, safe, and works cleanly across panel orientations, floating states, and fractional scales.

The diagnosis checks out against Panel.qml: PanelView's padding band (thick fixedMargins + smallSpacing) is wider than the margin applets actually get, so with 5 thin rows the Pager's whole top and bottom rows sat inside the band and every click or hover there was clamped onto a row gap. Leaving events alone when they already land on a visible applet fixes the real cause in the right place (PanelView), keeps Fitts' law for the empty edge pixels and the floating gap, and is a better fix than the pager spacing tweak in !3817. Mouse moves (hover), clicks, wheel and drag all go through containmentContainsPosition, so the whole report is covered. The before/after shots and the edge-click regression checks back this up. Nitpick: add #include <algorithm> for std::any_of instead of relying on a transitive include.
